entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPI(M) or CPM), founded in 1964 following a split with the Communist Party of India — is one of India's most significant left-wing political parties and one of the world's longest-governing communist parties in a democratic system, having ruled West Bengal continuously from 1977 to 2011 (34 years under the Left Front coalition) and Kerala multiple times, making these states extraordinary laboratories for democratic communist governance in a developing country.

The CPI(M)'s 34-year uninterrupted rule of West Bengal under the Left Front coalition was one of democracy's longest single-party or coalition dominances — eventually ended by Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress in 2011. The West Bengal government implemented land reform (Operation Barga, 1978-79 — registering approximately 1.4 million sharecroppers and securing their tenancy rights), decentralization through panchayati raj institutions, and literacy programs. Critics also noted increasing political violence, party machine entrenchment, and eventually the Singur and Nandigram controversies over industrial land acquisition.

Kerala under CPI(M) governance represents a different but equally significant achievement: Kerala has achieved extraordinary social development outcomes (near-universal literacy, high life expectancy, strong female education) that have been called the 'Kerala Model' — demonstrating that social investment through state policy can achieve developmental indicators comparable to wealthy countries even at low income levels. The 'Kerala Model' has been widely studied internationally as evidence of alternative development paths.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) — implementing the Kerala Model of social development and 34-year West Bengal governance — is historically significant as one of the world's most successful democratic communist parties and a living experiment in progressive governance within India's democratic system.
